title: Power Rankings: Nets, Pacers, Rockets shoot up the charts
heading: 2005-06 Power Rankings: Week 14

rankings.summaryHtml: When Chicago lost two straight in its 72-win season, it took Bulls from 41-3 to 41-5. Pistons' 2-2 week sets them back a bit farther; Detroit is at only a 70-win pace now.
rankings.summaryText: When Chicago lost two straight in its 72-win season, it took Bulls from 41-3 to 41-5. Pistons' 2-2 week sets them back a bit farther; Detroit is at only a 70-win pace now.

rankings.summaryHtml: With league's longest active win streak and only three more Ls than Detroit . . . you still won't hear any uproar about Dallas sending only one Mav to the All-Star Game.

rankings.summaryHtml: Spurs never sweat a stretch of eight straight roadies in February, but this (cushy?) Rodeo Road Trip comes with five days of rest back home after a 3-0 start.
rankings.summaryText: Spurs never sweat a stretch of eight straight roadies in February, but this (cushy?) Rodeo Road Trip comes with five days of rest back home after a 3-0 start.

rankings.summaryHtml: As valuable as Nash is -- again -- try not to ignore Marion. This is also the best Matrix we've ever seen, even if he continues to be underrated and taken for granted.

rankings.summaryHtml: It really would have been a special week had they won in Cleveland, too, but quality wins over Pistons and Heat stretch Nets' home unbeaten streak to 10.
rankings.summaryText: It really would have been a special week had they won in Cleveland, too, but quality wins over Pistons and Heat stretch Nets' home unbeaten streak to 10.

rankings.summaryHtml: Over .500 in February for just the fifth time in 36 seasons doesn't make this the best team in club history yet. My beloved Braves, don't forget, started 33-17 in '74-75.

rankings.summaryHtml: With Shaq back in Jersey, and Heat (seemingly) rolling at last, figured we'd see something big from the big guy. Try 11 points/six TOs vs. Collins and Uncle Cliffy.

rankings.summaryHtml: Last season's Cavs got to 30-20 before a 12-20 fold dropped them all the way out of the playoffs. These Cavs are hoping Hughes' return prevents a similar fold.

rankings.summaryHtml: Byron-bashers have no choice this time but to give the man his props. Unless you think Eddie Jordan is somehow pulling the strings from Washington.

rankings.summaryHtml: No slight to Pau and Co., but Grizz really aren't top-five material. And this comes, remember, from someone who liked them in the preseason more than most.

rankings.summaryHtml: Yes: 'Melo and Stevie Francis both have MD ties. But no: The idea of making them teammates (Furious George's idea, I'm told) holds no appeal at all to me.

rankings.summaryHtml: Just when you think 1-1/2 seasons of adversity had finally flattened these guys, O'Neal-less Pacers stun Detroit to remind everyone that they're still here.

rankings.summaryHtml: With competition like Rip, Vince, Pierce, Arenas and Kidd, it'll probably be easier for Redd to get Milwaukee to the playoffs than get himself to Houston.

rankings.summaryHtml: Odom can't be all bad, can he? Without him, Lakers suffer two lopsided losses (in Charlotte and OKC) to bring a hasty halt to the Kobe 4 MVP talk.

rankings.summaryHtml: Relax, panicky Philly fans. It has been a rocky season up to now, true, but recent history offers this for optimism: Webber hasn't missed the playoffs since 1998.

rankings.summaryHtml: Why do Rockets believe they can still leapfrog seven or eight teams to make the playoffs. They're 12-6 when T-Mac and Yao are healthy and, for now, both are.

rankings.summaryHtml: Even after a 10-5 uptick, Wiz haven't seen .500 since Dec. 6. The good news? Only two teams (Bulls, Magic) are realistically chasing them for the No. 8 spot.

rankings.summaryHtml: If we're going to keep zinging Atlanta for passing on CP3 (and we probably are) Jazz have to get it, too, for drafting a struggling Williams (Deron) of their own.

rankings.summaryHtml: The gamble on Artest sure didn't change Sacto's injury fortunes. Miller and Bonzi are dinged up again and even Artest is hobbling around.

rankings.summaryHtml: Wolves want to believe being on the road is what suddenly made them look so out of sorts. If not, their post-trade surge of momentum sure didn't last long.

rankings.summaryHtml: Everyone close to the situation says Monty's going nowhere, but the same can sadly be said about his unhappy team: Warriors are 9-19 since that 12-6 start.
